scope: Independent original-resolution pixel and source review of watchful servants01-03, Luke12:35-37; no import.

entries.alt: Two belted servants wait beside a closed wooden door at night, the older man holding a lit clay lamp while the younger attends toward the door.
entries.caption: The servants keep their lamps burning and their clothing gathered for work. Jesus uses this picture of readiness to invite watchful attention.
findings: Full-resolution original inspected: older bald gray-mustached blue-clad servant distinct from young dark-curled clean-shaven ochre servant; identities continue02/03.
Both waists belted; held clay lamp is level with flame away from fingers, shelf lamp steady. Hands/door touch plausible and night exterior with warm light coherent.
Young gaze directed toward door, elder toward younger is purposeful waiting rather than camera pose. No master, Christ or apostolic identity implied.
conditions: Characters and household setting illustrate the comparison, not literal Christ, named historical people or a documentary picture of the Second Coming.

entries.alt: A young servant holds the door open from inside while an older servant carries a lamp and their gray-bearded master stands outside the threshold.
entries.caption: The door opens to the returning master while the servants are ready to receive him. In Jesus' comparison, they wait so they can respond when he knocks.
findings: Same two servant identities and clothes preserved; third gray-bearded master clearly distinct in plum mantle. Young and master share welcoming gaze, older watches attentively.
View reads from inside toward night outside: young hand grips inner door edge while master stands beyond threshold. Door hardware/hand attachment and lamp support coherent.
Luke12:36 supplies return from wedding and prompt opening, though wedding/knock are not directly visible in still. Caption does not claim additional arrival event or literal Second Coming.
conditions: Characters and household setting illustrate the comparison, not literal Christ, named historical people or a documentary picture of the Second Coming.

entries.alt: The master, wearing a tied waist cloth over his cream tunic, sets a platter of bread before the two seated servants.
entries.caption: The master gathers his clothing for service and brings food to the seated servants. Jesus describes this unexpected welcome for those he finds watching.
findings: Master face matches02, now cream tunic with clearly tied waist cloth; he stands and serves while both established servants sit. Roles are unambiguously the reversal described inLuke12:37.
Master meets elder servant gaze; younger looks up toward master with warm attention. Expressions restrained, three distinct faces, no Christ substitute or Last Supper composition.
Both master hands support platter coherently; bread rests on it. Elder cup grip and tabletop objects have plausible physical contact; no floating food or extra hands.
Lamplight, skin, fabric and pottery remain photographic. Particular menu and room are artistic choices; service is source-supported.
conditions: Characters and household setting illustrate the comparison, not literal Christ, named historical people or a documentary picture of the Second Coming.
